layers.detail: Turns a question and a Unity Catalog table into a tested, governed MCP server
Budget books, SARs and contract records rebuilt as exact, cited tables
Researches a record that is missing data elements and names what to ask for
No figure reaches a product without deterministic checks; no model decides

layers.what: Front center, six agents, Genie Code skills
layers.detail: Pages that answer one question each; Ask the evidence calls the MCP servers; agents hand off through the work register
Calls every deployed server every 15 minutes with a known question

capabilities.name: MCP A Creator
capabilities.problem: Turning a dataset into a tool an agent can use takes a developer and weeks, and an improvised server is untested and different every time.
capabilities.does: Profiles the table, designs one tool per question, reviews meaning as well as shape, and generates a tested project that deploys as the requester's own app after an approval bound to what was reviewed.
capabilities.beyond: Every office with a Unity Catalog table and a question; GSA's stated aim of an internal library of MCP server prototypes.
capabilities.today: Built the ops server in this hub and, on an unrelated sales table, mcp-bakehouse-sales, rebuilt through its own tools in 0.38 s (7 tools, up from 4). 15 of 15 generated projects pass their own tests; output byte-identical across processes. Release 1.0.0rc1 with a changelog and SBOM, installable with uvx; every project records its spec, Creator version and file hashes, and mcp-a-creator-upgrade regenerates it without overwriting the owner's edits. Tested on FastMCP 3.4 and 4.2.

capabilities.name: Docs server
capabilities.problem: Budget justification books and SARs run to hundreds of pages, and analysts retype exhibits into spreadsheets.
capabilities.does: Maps each book by exhibit and budget line, rebuilds tables with exact decimals, ties out every subtotal and total, and says whether a figure appears in an authoritative or only a secondary source. No model.
capabilities.beyond: Budget analysts, cost estimators, congressional and GAO staff and auditors, on every appropriation's books and every program's SAR.
capabilities.today: 34 PDFs and 7,804 pages loaded; 7,743 of 7,746 tie-out checks pass over all 34 PDFs, the 3 left within rounding. Known answers at p50 1.18 s since the cache fix (12.6 s before). The reader has no CVN-79 logic.

capabilities.name: Analyst server
capabilities.problem: The slowest work in audit remediation is researching one record that is missing data elements: no contract, no line of accounting, no hull.
capabilities.does: Profiles what is missing, chases clues across FPDS, File C, sub-awards, the knowledge graph and the documents, weighs the evidence, and returns ranked cases with citations and a collection request for each missing element.
capabilities.beyond: Component reconciliation teams, DFAS, FIAR teams and auditors, on unsupported transactions and Universe of Transactions gaps.
capabilities.today: Reads the two CVN-79 prime contracts; attribution raised from 42.2% to 75.8% of the hull in one pass.

capabilities.name: Ops server
capabilities.problem: Agents need governed, paged, read-only access to facts without raw SQL.
capabilities.does: Exhibit cells, obligations on both prime contracts, the variance register, the knowledge graph and the work register, each through a validated tool.
capabilities.beyond: Any team that keeps its facts in Unity Catalog.
capabilities.today: Generated by the Creator, then edited by hand; golden set of 17 items with independent answers. Planted injection records: 15 of 16 answers correct, none followed the instruction.

capabilities.name: One Hub server (mcp-aircarrier-hub)
capabilities.problem: An AI agent can put a wrong figure in a leadership brief or a financial statement in one sentence.
capabilities.does: hub_check_claim routes any candidate figure through policy and the gate, against its own hull's total, and never promotes on its own; hub_challenge_text falsifies text against recorded error classes; hub_tie_out closes totals in exact decimals without a model; the gap tools turn every unknown into an owned request.
capabilities.beyond: Any office that lets an agent draft numbers: comptrollers, audit liaisons, budget shops.
capabilities.today: Deployed as a Databricks App on 2026-11-21 and watched by the probe: known answers right at p50 54 ms. Refuses a VERIFIED tag without a source and page, and a hull it has no total for (R9). An output schema on all 16 tools; 33 server tests; 193 hostile arguments, none leaked. Ask the evidence calls it over MCP.

capabilities.name: Probe
capabilities.problem: When an agent reports a failed connection, nobody can tell whether the server or the connector broke.
capabilities.does: Calls each server as a non-human caller through initialize, tools/list and one known-answer check, and logs which step failed.
capabilities.beyond: Any agency running MCP servers in production, as continuous monitoring evidence for an authority to operate.
capabilities.today: 413 sweeps, 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-20: 99.90% of 6,193 checks ok; 1,234 of 1,234 known answers right.

capabilities.name: Front center, agents, skills
capabilities.problem: Leaders and analysts need the answer, not the tools.
capabilities.does: Pages that each answer one question. Ask the evidence is an MCP host: it calls the docs, ops and One Hub servers (34 tools) and names the server behind each step. Six agents (investigator, reader, tie-out, challenger, attributor, briefer) hand work to each other only through the work register; three Genie Code skills.
capabilities.today: Live as a Databricks App: one question answered with four tool calls across three MCP servers. Also runs locally from the bundled data with two commands.

headline.n: Claude and GPT-5 mini with the servers, 1 of 10 without; ten sealed questions by an evaluator outside the development team
With the servers vs without, scored by a separate external reviewer who did not know which answer had tools
Every subtotal and total in 34 budget PDFs, in exact decimals, no model; the 3 left within rounding
Every deployed server called every 15 minutes; 99.90% of 6,193 checks ok

evaluation.measure: Subject-matter review: 10 round 4 answer pairs, scored blind by an external reviewer outside the development team
evaluation.result: 5.4 of 6 with the servers vs 1.0 without; would rely on 9 of 10 vs 0 of 10; preferred the servers' answer 10 of 10. The owner's own review: 5.4 vs 1.6
evaluation.not: One external reviewer, so no agreement statistic

evaluation.measure: Ten questions from an external evaluator (a PEO office) outside the development team, sealed by SHA-256 on receipt (round 5)
evaluation.result: Claude Sonnet 4.5 25/30 (83.3%), GPT-5 mini 19/30 (63.3%; 21/30 read by hand); 1/10 each without tools. Exhibit questions 30 of 30 for both
evaluation.not: Ten questions; misses cluster on a source the servers do not hold and an eight-turn limit

evaluation.measure: Sealed held-out questions, round 4, 69 questions, three repeats
evaluation.not: Questions drawn by a seeded generator or drafted by Genie Code and reviewed by the project owner

evaluation.measure: Round 4 accuracy by the server of the first tool call
evaluation.result: Claude 87.2% from docs, 89.7% from ops; GPT-5 mini 75.2% and 84.0%
evaluation.not: The first call shows where a run started, not every server it used

evaluation.measure: Sealed held-out questions, round 3, with vs without tools
evaluation.not: Questions written by the same author as the fixes; read by hand, 55/72

evaluation.measure: Sealed held-out questions, round 2, with vs without tools
evaluation.not: Run before the fixes it prompted; 28 of 41 misses needed a tool that did not exist yet

evaluation.measure: Tool choice, round 1: 14 questions, 29 tools at once
Hostile arguments against all 30 read tools and the Creator
evaluation.result: 421 calls to the read servers: 340 refused, none wrote, none pasted into SQL; 400 to the Creator: nothing written outside its root
evaluation.not: In-process against a recording fake warehouse
Determinism is not correctness; the review checks meaning

evaluation.measure: Latency after the docs cache fix, 2026-11-22
evaluation.result: Docs: 233 of 234 right across a cache expiry, p50 1.18 s, max 2.34 s (12 to 20 s before). Hub: p50 54 ms in the probe
evaluation.not: One night, one workspace; laptop network time included in the docs run

evaluation.measure: Tie-outs on the deployed store, all 34 PDFs
evaluation.result: 7,743 of 7,746 checks pass; the 3 left within the rounding bound of the printed figures
evaluation.not: Ties a table to itself; says nothing about whether the book was right
A budget estimate, not an audited cost

evaluation.measure: Code suites from a clean clone
evaluation.result: 1,649 passed, 0 failed, 825 of them hostile-input cases (9 projects)
evaluation.not: Tests show the code does what it says, not that it helps a user

security.control: Identifiers allow-listed and quoted; values bound as parameters; 421 hostile calls, none pasted into SQL
Free text made inert; eight payloads fuzzed; every generated file compiled with warnings as errors; 400 hostile calls to the Creator, nothing written outside its root
Read-only tools except one gated label write; Creator writes are dry runs; deploy needs an approval token bound to the reviewed design
Per-user OAuth through Databricks Apps; tables read as the caller under Unity Catalog; the MCP host sends its token only to a Databricks Apps host at /mcp; no credentials in code
Retrieved text is data, never instructions; any result holding text aimed at a model carries a source notice; planted records: 15 of 16 answers correct, none followed
Every server returns a failure as isError with its reason and a hint, so a client never counts an error as an answer
pip-audit and bandit in CI and in every generated project; FastMCP 3.4 or later, which closes two published CVEs
